v: A one-hour transformation from ‘What the F***’ to ‘WHAT A F***’ 😄 The romance nearly lost me, but once the film shifts gears it becomes a BANG, with Chaitanya’s best performance till then and a climax I actually loved.
e: Sahasam Swasaga Sagipo is a sharply divided experience for me: the romantic first hour was painful because that genre rarely works for me, while the later semi-action stretch suddenly becomes gripping. Naga Chaitanya gives what I felt was his best performance to that point, the BGM is superb and the much-criticised climax actually felt realistic to me.
body:
What an awesome transformation from “What the F***” to “WHAT A F***!!!!!” 😄

And no, the four-letter word does not stand for FILM 😛

The first hour was horrible for me.

That is partly personal because I am simply not a fan of the romance genre, and the early stretch leans heavily into exactly that zone.

But after that… BANG!!!!!

The movie suddenly shifts gears and becomes much more engaging.

I saw several reviews saying the climax was weak, but personally I loved it.

In fact, I thought the way it resolved the situation felt more realistic than the giant heroic ending many films would have chosen.

Undoubtedly, this was Naga Chaitanya’s best performance for me till that point.

Manjima Mohan fits the role well, and the supporting characters also feel appropriate rather than distracting.

The BGM is superb.

The music itself is okay — again, I am not the biggest fan of Rahman’s slower romantic songs — and I had my usual complaints about some of the lyrics.

The funny part is that Vellipomakey almost sounds like the film itself talking to the audience during that first hour: “Vellipomakandi… stay here, the movie is going to become superb after this” 😛

Overall, it is a good movie for viewers who enjoy a romance-to-action transition and can survive that opening stretch.

Whatever my genre bias, I did feel the central concept and story were grounded in realism right from the beginning.

v: I usually get bored by pure romance, yet Premam kept me engaged — largely because Praveen’s comedy keeps the emotions light. Think Naa Autograph minus the heavy sentiment, plus easy entertainment.
e: I had not watched the Malayalam original, so I entered the Telugu Premam without comparison baggage. Naga Chaitanya delivers one of his better performances, Shruti Haasan is effortless, the music and visuals suit the story, and Praveen’s comedy becomes the crucial ingredient that keeps a romance-averse viewer like me happily involved.
body:
I had not watched the original Malayalam version, so my reaction to Premam was not pre-programmed by comparisons.

Four people especially stood out to me.

Naga Chaitanya clearly tries his best and, for the most part, succeeds in giving one of his strongest performances till then.

He also looks stylish across the other stages of the character’s life.

Praveen, to be frank, carries a huge portion of the movie through his comedy timing and expressions.

That contribution was particularly important for me because pure romantic films usually start making me feel bored very quickly 😄

Srinivas plays an important role during the final half hour, while Shruti Haasan handles her character with complete ease.

The music and BGM are good and suit the plot nicely.

The visuals in the Evare song are especially delightful to watch.

The dialogues are also very good.

I particularly liked the thought that love, hatred and anger are all feelings — we may want those feelings to grow, but whether they remain can depend on the other person too.

To cut it short: love and romance movies have always had the power to bore me, but Premam keeps me engaged because it constantly balances the romance with entertainment.

Without the comedy I might have had a completely different reaction.

For me, it is almost Naa Autograph minus the heavy emotions plus light-hearted comedy.

v: Pure Puri markISM — his dialogue bombs have graduated into MISSILES 😄 The second half is racy, Kalyan Ram is uber-cool and excellent, and Puri fans should absolutely watch it… though it is time he borrowed someone else’s story once in a while.
e: ISM is unmistakably Puri Jagannadh, built around aggressive one-liners, attitude and a much tighter second half. Kalyan Ram looks completely at ease and gives especially strong work later in the film. I enjoyed the Puri flavour enough to recommend it to his audience, even while feeling increasingly that his writing would benefit from bringing other storytellers into the room.
body:
This is purely PURI markISM!!!!!

Movie after movie, Puri Jagannadh’s dialogue bombs seem to be upgrading themselves into MISSILES 😄

The language is unapologetically Puri — angry, provocative, funny and sometimes deliberately vulgar.

Whether he is talking about the farmer who grows everyone’s food, corruption by people who look exactly like us, attraction, or a stupid misunderstanding around the word “duck,” the lines arrive with that unmistakable Puri rhythm.

The second half is racy and to the point, and that is where the movie works best for me.

At the same time, I really do feel it is time for Puri to start taking stories from other writers occasionally.

His voice is still powerful, but the basic story foundations would benefit from somebody else bringing fresh material into that voice.

Kalyan Ram is uber-cool and delivers excellent acting, particularly in the second half.

He looks completely comfortable with the attitude and energy the film demands.

Bottom line: worth watching if you enjoy Puri-mark cinema.

Migitha vaallu Brahmotsavam ki velli manchi maatalu vinandi 😄

v: A different, mature concept carried by understated emotions and strong performances. It may feel much longer than its two hours to a regular audience, but lovers of unusual cinema should give it a one-time watch.
e: Mana Oori Ramayanam has a distinctive single-point premise and deliberately avoids loud dialogue or commercial decoration. Prakash Raj and Priyamani are predictably strong, while Prudhvi surprises with a serious, mature performance and Ilaiyaraaja’s music fits the restrained mood. Its slow, subtle approach will not connect with everyone, but the experiment deserves appreciation.
body:
A different story and concept with emotions running quietly underneath!!!!!

Prakash Raj and Priyamani nail their performances — which, frankly, is exactly what you expect from actors of their calibre.

The surprise for me is Prudhvi.

After years of seeing the “30 Years Industry” comedy image, watching him deliver a serious, mature performance adds another dimension to the film.

The movie is hardly two hours long, yet a normal audience may feel as though it is running for ages.

That is because the film stays focused on a single point and works through subtle emotion rather than heavy dialogues, comedy tracks or constant dramatic turns.

Ilaiyaraaja’s music is good and fits the material well without trying to overpower it.

Even though the movie received a clean U certificate, I can imagine many viewers not connecting with the mature and somewhat bold core concept.

So hats off to Prakash Raj for taking that kind of storyline and still moulding it into a clean film.

For regular commercial audiences, this may be a difficult sit.

For movie lovers who actively encourage different concepts, it is worth a one-time watch.
